title: hx-get & hx-post: Declarative AJAX & HX-Request Headers

progressiveExplaining.eli5: In traditional web pages, only links (`<a>`) can fetch new pages and only `<form>` tags can send data. HTMX lets ANY HTML tag (buttons, divs, dropdowns) send a request to the server and swap the incoming HTML fragment directly into the page without reloading.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `hx-get` and `hx-post` trigger AJAX requests directly from HTML attributes: `<button hx-get="/api/users" hx-target="#list">Load</button>`. HTMX intercepts the click, sends an AJAX request with custom headers (like `HX-Request: true`), and swaps the returned HTML string into `#list` (`innerHTML` by default).
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `hx-get` and `hx-post` embrace the REST/HATEOAS hypermedia model: the server returns HTML partials (hypermedia state transitions) rather than raw JSON, eliminating client-side template compilation and JSON schema duplication. HTMX automatically injects headers (`HX-Request`, `HX-Target`, `HX-Current-URL`) allowing backend endpoints to conditionally return full layout pages or minimal partials based on the calling context.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: HTMX attaches event listeners (via event delegation) on the `document.body`. When an element with `hx-get`/`hx-post` triggers, it creates an `XMLHttpRequest` or `fetch`, sets request headers (`HX-Request: true`), issues the request, parses the returned HTML text via `DOMParser` or range fragments, and dispatches lifecycle events (`htmx:beforeRequest`, `htmx:afterOnLoad`, `htmx:afterSettle`).

interviewGotchas.question: How can a backend endpoint distinguish between a full browser navigation and an HTMX AJAX request?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of HTMX request header inspection for backend conditional rendering.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: HTMX automatically sends the **`HX-Request: true`** HTTP header on every AJAX request. Server-side controllers inspect this header: if present, the server renders and returns only the minimal HTML partial (e.g. `<tr>...</tr>`); if absent (e.g. initial direct browser page load), the server renders the full page template including `<head>`, `<body>`, and navigation bars.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Failing to check `HX-Request` on endpoints serving both direct visits and HTMX partials will cause the entire HTML page layout to be nested inside the target element.

interviewGotchas.question: What is the default trigger event for `hx-get` on different HTML elements?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of natural event triggers in HTMX.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: HTMX assigns default triggers based on element semantics: `<input>`, `<textarea>`, and `<select>` trigger on the `change` event; `<form>` triggers on the `submit` event; all other elements (like `<button>`, `<div>`, `<a>`) trigger on the `click` event.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: You can override any default trigger using `hx-trigger="mouseenter"` or `hx-trigger="keyup changed delay:500ms"`.
